To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sparsomycin crosslinks to A2602 of the peptidly transferase loop of 23S rRNA, in a complex with an N-blocked tRNA, but not with deacylated tRNAs.

(i) sparsomycin binds to the peptidlyl transferase loop region in the presence of N-blocked tRNA; (ii) the crosslink is formed with the universally conserved rRNA nucleotide A2603; and (iii) the antibiotic crosslinks to A2603 only when the tRNA substrate is present.

sparsomycin crosslinks exclusively to A2602, which is a universally conserved residue in the peptitlyl transferase loop region in the peptilyl transferase loop of rRNA in the ribosomal P-site; and the crosslink is induced by an N-blocked tRNA substrate and is inhibited by several other inhibitors of peptide bond formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of sparsomycin as a universal and selective inhibitor of peptide bond synthesis in ribosomes.
the identification of the site of action of sparsomycin in ribosome-tRNA complex and the role of the antibiotic in the peptyltransferase reaction.
the first direct demonstration of the interaction of a ribosomal antibiotic with A2602 within 23S-like ribosomal RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sparsomycin binds at a site on the ribosome where it induces a conformational switch in the peptido-transferase loop of the 23S-like ribosomal RNA that is essential for the peptido-transferring activity of the ribosome.
sparsomycin binds to the ribosomal A site and induces a conformational switch in the peptyl transferase center, which prevents formation of the peptidic bond.
sparsomycin binds to the ribosomal peptidyl site and that the antibiotic crosslink to A2602 is induced by the conformational switch that is induced by the binding of the N-blocked P-tRNA substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
A2602 is the target for sparsomycin on the ribosome, and that the antibiotic binds to the ribosomes of all organisms in the presence of a donor tRNA substrate.
A2602 in 23S-like ribosomal RNA is a target for sparsomycin in ribosome-tRNA ternary complexes.

sparsomycin crosslinks with A2602 of the peptidyt transferase loop in the presence of N-blocked P-tRNA, and that this crosslink is a consequence of the interaction of the antibiotic with the ribosome and the tRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sparsomycin binds to a site on the ribosome that is close to A2602, and this site is essential both for peptidyl-transferase activity and for sparsomycin action.
the crosslinking method is a valuable tool for studying antibiotic action and the mechanism of peptide bond formation.
